anomalies: There are no non-200 or stream_error rows in any cell of the formal ledger, and retried_stream_errors adds up to 0. 4 rows have status 200 but usage and cost are both null, so their cost is missing from the totals (a small undercount of unknown size): formal-g4-on-A-72, formal-g4-on-C-2697, and 2 rows of the superseded formal-g4-on-C-43 run. One of the C-43 rows also has provider=None and generation_id=None. Those 2 C-43 rows are the last requests before that run was killed by SIGTERM/KeyboardInterrupt (logs/43-g4-on-C.log).
One row (formal-q38-on-A-38) has attempts=2, meaning an HTTP-level retry. Its cost is recorded ($0.00081344).

The superseded original g4-C-43 run spent $0.00957861 across 13 requests (about 1% of the gemma C cost). It stays in the all-rows totals but is left out of the counted-trial totals. The original g4-C-50 run failed with AgentSetupTimeoutError and made 0 model requests. The first 43 rerun attempt (log 43-g4-on-C-r2.log) died with FileExistsError on the job directory and made no requests; the r2b attempt is the one in job dir 20-10-15 (reruns.json labels both dirs 'r2', and the ledger tag is -r2).

There is a hard cap of 15 requests per trial. For gemma it bites hard: 36/79 A trials and 45/79 C trials hit it, and 38/79 C trials never reached Stop, so Vacant never ran its check on them. The gemma cost difference is therefore squeezed by the cap and does not show how much C would cost with no cap.

All 7 gemma trials that Vacant sent back (review_actions=['continue']) ran on to the 15-request cap without ever getting an allow. The extra cost of those 7 (+49.6%) is spend after being sent back that ended without a pass.

Gemma trials where Vacant only said allow still cost 18.0% more in C than in A (33 tasks). An allow adds no requests, and the first request's prompt is the same size in A and C on all 79 tasks. So this gap is run-to-run variance in the agent's path, not overhead from Vacant. The overall C-over-A percentage mixes that variance with any real effect, and it swings with the basis: gemma is +8.54% on 77 tasks, +8.70% on 79 counted trials, and +9.75% on all rows.
Tasks 5 and 70 behave the opposite way from the main set for qwen: C costs 44.7% less than A. For gemma C costs 14.4% more. These rest on tiny samples (2 tasks each).

reasoning_tokens looks like a subset of completion_tokens (for example completion 124 with reasoning 110), so the two should not be added together. Only qwen has cached_tokens (prompt cache hits); gemma's is 0 everywhere.

mismatches: Cost is counted on a different basis from the scores. The reported figures (gemma A $0.9174/974 req, C $1.0068/1038 req, +9.7%; qwen A $0.6186/557, C $0.6577/547, +6.3%) match R2 exactly, but only on its 'all formal ledger rows' basis. That basis covers all 79 tasks, including 5 and 70, and it also includes the discarded gemma C-43 run (13 requests, $0.0096). The scores use 77 tasks. On the same 77 tasks (R2): gemma A $0.8914 (951 req) vs C $0.9675 (1001 req), +8.5%; qwen A $0.5999 (541 req) vs C $0.6474 (535 req), +7.9%. So the reported basis overstates gemma's extra cost and understates qwen's; on the 77 tasks, qwen's C costs more than the reported +6.3%.

'gemma C reached stop check 41/81 runs' puts the 2 discarded runs in the denominator: 43 was killed after 13 requests and 50 made 0 requests. The qwen figure (78/79) does not. On the same basis the gemma figure is 41/79 over the 79 scored runs, or 40/77 on the 77-task set (R3: 40 reached, 37 not). The qwen equivalent on 77 tasks is 76/77. The numerator 41 is correct: I checked, and neither discarded run has a review.

're-run once' is not quite accurate for task 43. It was re-run twice. The first attempt (dir 20-07-41, log 43-g4-on-C-r2.log) failed at once with FileExistsError because it collided with task 50's re-run directory, and it made 0 requests. The second attempt (dir 20-10-15) is the one that counted. reruns.json labels both 'r2'. The prereg (section 3) says 'if the re-run also breaks, drop the pair'. Read strictly, that drops pair 43 and makes n=76. The McNemar result would not change, because 43 is wrong in both arms (A and C), but the denominators would.

'Provider errors 0' holds for formal rows (non-200 and stream_error are 0). But 4 status-200 rows have null usage and null cost, so the cost totals are slightly low: g4-A-72, g4-C-2697, and 2 rows of the discarded g4-C-43 run. One row (q38-A-38) was retried once at the HTTP level (attempts=2). The 12 failed requests in summary.json are all in non-formal tags.
unsupported: 'All qwen flips and 15/16 gemma flips were C runs never sent back' is literally true but misleading. For 10 of the 11 gemma only-A flips (12, 21, 23, 28, 32, 40, 44, 59, 61, 1871), the C run hit the 15-request cap and never reached the stop check. I checked the verifier output: all 10 say '/app/answer.txt not found'. Vacant never looked at these runs. It did not look and approve them. Only 68 was reviewed, allowed, and wrong.

'7 of 8 push-backs were on answers already correct' understates the problem. R3 shows from the raw records that all 8 push-backs were false positives. 5 'unsourced' values (tasks 11, 25, 33, 38, 1753) appear word for word in earlier bash output in Vacant's own chain. 73.150 (task 6) is 73.1495… rounded. Both failed_step cases (gemma 62, qwen 40) were grep returning exit 1 because it found nothing. The one push-back on a wrong answer (gemma 1753) flagged the wrong thing: 868 is sourced, and the actual error is the missing id 939.

'harm = 0' is true only under the prereg's narrow definition (correct at the first stop, wrong after push-back). It says nothing about the push-backs using up turns. On gemma, the 7 sent-back runs had 1–6 requests left, all 7 ran to the 15 cap, and none reached a second check. 3 of the 9 extra cap hits in C (tasks 6, 11, 25) are on sent-back runs. Their answers were already written, so they still scored correct.
missing_for_decision: The check was changed after the results were seen, and the summary does not say so. Commit efda0d1f changed trace/evidence.py after the formal batch: program output now counts as a source, and grep/rg finding nothing no longer counts as a failed step. Its regression tests are taken from formal tasks 25, 62 and 40. The commit says that, replayed on the recorded runs, none of the 8 push-backs would fire. Nobody has checked that independently. If it is true, the current code would have allowed every stop in this batch without a single push-back, so on this benchmark it would have had no effect at all. The version that was evaluated (prereg commit 8b22c7cc) is not the current code. Because the fix was tuned on these same 79 tasks, re-running them would not be an independent test.

Vacant caught zero wrong answers. 14 wrong answers were allowed: qwen 12 (17, 18, 36, 43, 47, 49, 60, 61, 71, 1273, 1753, 1871) and gemma 2 (67, 68). They include qwen 1753, where answer.txt was an empty string. The 'required file does not exist' check does not catch an empty file.

Structural limit: the check only runs when the agent says it is done, and push-backs count toward the 15-request cap. That cap is binding for gemma in both arms (A 35/77, C 44/77 hit it). So nearly half the gemma C runs (37/77) were never checked, and any push-back had almost no requests left to fix anything. With this setup, gemma mostly measures running out of turns, not Vacant's check.

Where the gemma gap comes from: C wrote no answer.txt in 28 runs vs 25 in A, and gave a wrong answer in 5 vs 2. Why C hits the cap more often (+9 runs, only 3 linked to push-back) is unexplained. The first request's prompt tokens are identical in A and C on all 79 tasks, so nothing was injected. That points to run-to-run variance, but with one run per task per arm, variance cannot be separated from an effect. Cost shows the same noise: gemma tasks where Vacant only allowed still cost 18% more in C, with no Vacant action. So the extra-cost percentages mix variance with any real overhead.

Sample size: there are only 16 (gemma) and 8 (qwen) flipped tasks. p=0.21 and 0.29, both leaning A ≥ C. The prereg fixes the wording in advance: 'this round measured no difference', not 'no effect' and not 'harm'. The prereg's only primary comparison is gemma. qwen is secondary and descriptive, but the summary presents the two side by side as equals.

The prereg (section 4) requires reporting wall-clock time per task for both arms. That is missing from the summary and from all three recomputations. It also requires a prompt/completion/reasoning token breakdown. R2 has it, but the summary reports only dollars and request counts.
Tasks 5 and 70: 'A 1/2, C 1/2' hides that task 5 was correct in all four runs and task 70 was wrong in all four (expected 'Not Applicable'; three runs answered 'yes', gemma A wrote no answer).

Problems in the recomputations themselves. (a) R3 says that among the 10 cap-hit only-A gemma flips, '9 wrote no answer', but its own flip table shows no C answer for all 10, and the verifier output confirms 10/10 had answer.txt not found. R3's '9' is wrong. (b) R1 says the original task-43 agent 'finished'. R2 says it was killed by SIGTERM after 13 requests, with the last 2 rows missing cost. R2 is more specific, and either way discarding the run is justified. (c) R3 saw the conclusion in a commit message partway through its work (it disclosed this). It says its numbers were computed before that point.
result.verdict: Every number in the report reproduces exactly on some basis. The score, flip, McNemar, cap-hit, push-back-count, harm, and budget figures agree across all three recomputations. There are no outright numeric errors. There are four accuracy problems: (1) Cost uses all ledger rows (79 tasks plus the discarded run), while scores use 77 tasks. On 77 tasks the extra cost is gemma +8.5% and qwen +7.9%, not +9.7% and +6.3%. (2) The gemma stop-check rate 41/81 puts discarded runs in the denominator; the comparable figures are 41/79 or 40/77. (3) Task 43 was re-run twice, not once; the first attempt crashed with FileExistsError. Under a strict reading of the prereg rule the pair would be dropped, which changes denominators but not p. (4) 'Never sent back' hides that 10 of 11 gemma A-only flips were never checked at all: they hit the cap and wrote no answer. Several things that matter for the decision are left out: all 8 push-backs were false positives, and 0 of 14 wrong answers were caught (one was an empty answer file). The check was changed after the results were seen, using this same eval set, so the current code would reportedly have done nothing on this batch. The 15-request cap left about half the gemma C runs unchecked, and gave any push-back almost no room to fix anything. One run per task cannot separate variance from effect. Wall-clock time, which the prereg requires, is not reported.
